The degradation has one root cause: `ts-order-other-service`, specifically its database query path on pod `ts-order-other-service-677c8677b5-rwk4f`. Its slow work propagates upward to the user-facing requests. No request errors or 5xx responses appear anywhere; the impact is latency only.

## Affected endpoints and services (abnormal vs normal)

| Service | Abnormal avg / p95 | Normal avg / p95 |
|---|---|---|
| loadgenerator / ts-ui-dashboard (entry) | ~780 ms / ~3.1 s | ~74 ms / ~0.2 s |
| ts-travel-plan-service | 3.4 s / 16.5 s | 159 ms / 651 ms |
| ts-travel2-service | 1.3 s / 5.7 s | 35 ms / 102 ms |
| ts-route-plan-service | 2.4 s / 11.1 s | 153 ms / 562 ms |
| ts-preserve-service | 1.2 s / 4.1 s | 278 ms / 1.5 s |
| ts-seat-service | 725 ms / 2.8 s | 15 ms / 20 ms |
| ts-security-service | 779 ms / 2.8 s | 9 ms / 26 ms |
| ts-order-other-service | 2.4 s / 2.8 s | 3.8 ms / 7 ms |

The user-facing endpoints are the UI-dashboard routes for travel planning, travel2, preserve, and order-other refresh.

## Root cause

**`ts-order-other-service` database access is slow.**
- Its DB spans are the hotspot: `SELECT ts.orders_other` averages about 1.33 s (normal about 1.1 ms), and `SELECT Order` averages about 2.7 s (normal about 1.7 ms).
- Its repository spans (`findByTravelDateAndTrainNumber`, `findByAccountId`) and its controller spans (`getTicketListByDateAndTripId`, `queryOrdersForRefresh`, `securityInfoCheck`) all sit at 2.6 to 2.8 s.
- Self-time, meaning span duration minus child-span duration, is about 541 ms on average versus 1.6 ms normally. This is the only service whose own work changed.
- The slowdown began around 12:10 and held flat at about 1.38 s per query through 12:14. That looks like a fixed delay on the query path, not a load ramp.
- CPU, thread count, and heap were not saturated. Container CPU was about 619 versus 588 normally, and threads matched normal. This points to the DB access path, not compute.
- Pool metrics looked the same as normal, so I did not find evidence of connection-pool exhaustion.
- Every slow order-other span is on the single pod above.

## Propagation path

Each upstream span's duration almost exactly equals the order-other child duration, so these services are passing the wait through:
- `ts-order-other-service` is called by `ts-seat-service` (about 2.66 s), `ts-security-service` (about 2.57 s), and directly by `ts-ui-dashboard` (about 2.8 s).
- `ts-seat-service` is called by `ts-travel2-service` (about 2.66 s) and `ts-travel-plan-service` (about 1.1 s).
- `ts-security-service` is called by `ts-preserve-service` (about 2.6 s), which in turn is called by `ts-ui-dashboard` (about 3.5 s).
- `ts-route-plan-service` calls `ts-travel2-service` (about 2.9 s). `ts-travel-plan-service` calls `ts-route-plan-service` (about 6.5 s).
- `ts-ui-dashboard` calls `ts-travel-plan-service` (about 12 s) and `ts-travel2-service` (about 6.1 s).
- `loadgenerator` calls `ts-ui-dashboard` (p95 about 3.1 s versus 0.2 s normally).

## Ruled out

- **ts-food-service `createFoodOrder`** (about 1.2 s): this is baseline behavior. Normal data shows about 1.37 s for the same span.
- **ts-config-service** (one 1.5 s span at 12:12): an isolated outlier, not systemic.
- **Log errors:** the RabbitMQ auto-delete errors in notification and delivery services also appear in normal data. The "No content" WARNs in order-other are also present in normal data (788 normal versus 95 abnormal), so they are not discriminating.
